verses.text: The LORD sent Nathan to David. Nathan came in and said, “Two men lived in the same city. One was rich and the other was poor.
The rich man owned many flocks and herds.

The poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb he had bought. He raised her, and she grew up with him and his children. She ate his food, drank from his cup, and curled up in his arms. She was like a daughter to him.
A traveler came to visit the rich man. The rich man wouldn't take an animal from his own flock or herd to cook for his guest. He took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the traveler.”
David was furious. “As surely as the LORD lives,” he told Nathan, “the man who did this deserves to die!
He has to pay back four times what he took, because he did this without a shred of pity!”
Nathan told David, “You're that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel and rescued you from Saul.
I gave you your master's household and his wives, and I gave you Israel and Judah. If that had been too little, I'd have given you even more.
Why did you treat the LORD's word with contempt and do what he sees as evil? You struck down Uriah the Hittite and took his wife as your own. You used the sword of the Ammonites to kill him.
So now the sword will never leave your family, because you treated me with contempt and took Uriah the Hittite's wife as your own.’

“This is what the LORD says: ‘I will bring trouble against you from within your own family. Right in front of you I will take your wives and give them to someone close to you, and he will sleep with them in broad daylight.
You did this in secret, but I will do this in broad daylight before all Israel.’”
David told Nathan, “I've sinned against the LORD.” Nathan replied, “The LORD has taken away your sin. You won't die.
But what you did gave the LORD's enemies plenty of reason to speak against him. The child born to you will surely die.”
Then Nathan went home. The LORD struck the child Uriah's wife had borne to David, and the child became very sick.
David pleaded with God for the child. He fasted, went inside, and lay on the ground all night.
The elders of his household stood beside him and tried to help him up, but he refused to get up or eat with them.

On the seventh day the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him. “When the child was alive, he wouldn't listen to us,” they said. “What if he hurts himself when we tell him the child is dead?”
David saw his servants whispering and realized what had happened. “Is the child dead?” he asked. They said, “He is.”
David got up from the ground, washed, put oil on himself, and changed his clothes. He went to the LORD's house to worship. Then he went home, asked for food, and ate what they brought him.
His servants asked, “Why are you doing this? While the child was alive you fasted and cried. Now that he's dead, you've gotten up and eaten.”
David said, “While the child was alive, I fasted and cried because I thought, ‘Who knows? The LORD might show me mercy and let the child live.’
But now he's dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back? I'll go to him, but he won't come back to me.”
David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. She gave birth to a son, and David named him Solomon. The LORD loved him.
The LORD sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah, because the LORD loved him.
Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah in Ammon and seized the royal city.
Joab sent messengers to David: “I've fought against Rabbah and captured the part of the city that controls its water.
Now gather the rest of the troops, surround the city, and take it yourself. Otherwise I'll take it and the city will be called by my name.”
So David gathered all the troops, went to Rabbah, fought against it, and captured it.
David took the crown off their king's head. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones. It was placed on David's head, and he took a great deal of plunder out of the city.

David brought the people out and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and iron axes, and made them work at the brick kiln. He did this in all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all the troops returned to Jerusalem.
